name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network patches on dirt ground (flat ground tiles)

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain tileset sheet, not a standing object. It shows dark asphalt road segments (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a large block) on a brown dirt ground, all seen straight from above. The 256-wide silhouette is fully opaque from rows 0-191. The column scans show only texture variation (cracks, aggregate) and no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical front face. The darker broken lip along the road edges is a ground-transition detail and not a south face. Since the kind is terrain, the image is a flat top-down ground surface with no standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile. The asphalt ramp is shallow, with roughly 3 steps: a mid slate, a darker slate and a few light speckles. The dirt surround is brown with about 3 tones of mottled blotches. The paving reference reaches 7 visible tones and the grass 3 visible tones with 26 raw colours, so the candidate sits between them on the numbers. Near-flat coverage is 4%, so there are no large flat fills, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted. The crumbling edges are dark slate and brown rather than black, so they read as material-tone. Weaknesses: the asphalt body is a uniform mottle, the hairline cracks, repair patch and oil stain are barely visible, and the loose chunks are sparse. The dirt texture is a repeating pattern rather than shaded clumps. Overall it is cleanly drawn but shallower than the 5-6 step Beodeul standard on each material, so it is borderline-shallow and I fail it when in doubt.
